title: Bram and the Postcard
premise: Kestrel Iversen fled a scandal that cost him his reputation and a fiancé who chose duty over love, rebuilding himself as a turtle-counting marine biologist on a quiet coast. When he inherits a share of an orchard deed co-owned with Bram Aldous—the postcard-writing stranger whose letters kept him sane through his worst years—he discovers the man behind the words is the same lawyer now representing the developer trying to seize the orchard. Forced into legal and emotional opposition, they fall for each other across negotiation tables and tide pools until Kestrel must choose between testifying to save the orchard (and torching his fragile new career) or staying silent and safe. He testifies, the community rallies to save the land, and Bram walks away from the firm; the book ends with the two of them planting a tree where the postcards always said home was.
about_author: Lior Sterling is a former coastal field researcher who traded data loggers for love stories set against working landscapes. They write about people who rebuild themselves in small, stubborn increments.

chapters.title: The Deed with Two Names
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A probate letter reveals his late aunt left him half of Hollow Orchard—co-owned with a stranger named Bram Aldous, the sender of three years of unsigned postcards Kestrel never answered. Shocked and defensive, Kestrel drives up intending to sell his share immediately, but finds the orchard thriving and someone clearly living there. Emotional beat: guarded curiosity cracking open old loneliness.

chapters.title: What the Postcards Never Said
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Kestrel learns Bram is the postcard writer—and the attorney for Meridian Development, which wants the orchard for a marina. Their first meeting is frost and fascination: Bram confesses he wrote anonymously out of guilt over the firm's earlier role in Kestrel's downfall. They agree to a 60-day truce to find an alternative. Emotional beat: wary attraction tangled with betrayal.

chapters.title: High Water Mark
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. As surveys and town meetings escalate, Bram secretly builds Kestrel's legal defense while falling deeper—shared nights tagging turtles, a kiss in the rain-soaked rows. Then Meridian uncovers Kestrel's past scandal and threatens to expose him unless he sells cheap. Bram must choose his firm or Kestrel, and hesitates one day too long. Emotional beat: love colliding with duty at maximum pressure.

chapters.title: Where Home Was
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Hurt but resolute, Kestrel testifies publicly about Meridian's coercion, sacrificing his anonymity and risking his career; the town and his found family of researchers rally, and the county denies the marina permit. Bram resigns from the firm and arrives at the orchard with an answered stack of every postcard. They plant a sapling together as the epilogue of letters closes. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, and choosing love without apology.
